newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF, Lagardere shares hit at Paris open.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF, Lagardere shares hit at Paris open.

text.p: Shares in defence electronics giant Thomson-CSF and missiles firm Lagardere fell at the Paris stock market opening on Tuesday after the government announced late on Friday it was scrapping a privatisation of Thomson-CSF.

Thomson-CSF fell 3.18 percent to open at 164.2 francs after the long Bastille Day weekend. Lagardere, which had put in a bid to buy the company, fell 3.91 percent to 172 francs on press speculation its rival Alcatel Alsthom was preferred as a minority partner. Alcatel rose 1.7 percent to 778 francs.
The CAC-40 blue chip index was up 16.05 points or 0.55 percent at 2957.64 in early trading on volume of more than one billion francs.
Dealers said stocks were lifted by the dollar and a catch-up effect on gains made on other stock exchanges during the Paris holiday on Monday.
France's new elected Socialist-led government said after the markets closed on Friday that it was calling off the sale of a 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF.
It said a new procedure to be launched soon would include a "decisive" but unspecified state shareholding in what would be a new pole for the French defence electronics industry.
